paraphrase: In one two-atom truth/falsity-pair semantics, K3 validates g⊢p but LP does not, LP validates excluded middle e for q but K3 does not, and both validate conjunction introduction. For g=p∨(q∧¬q) and C=p∧e, neither validates g⊢C. Every SAME selected pool containing g and closed under both relations contains C. Each of the three input conditions can be omitted with the others retained and C rejected; both closure omissions are closed semantic theories, and the initial-acceptance omission is a classical designated pool. A common closed nontrivial pool rejects ¬p, and separately indexed K3/LP pools each contain g and reject C. These are conditional policy and matrix results, not categorical authority, validity collapse, join=CPL or a refutation of pluralism.
